Temperature.description:
Probability threshold for nucleus sampling during the generation procedure.

> - For example, when the value is 0.8, only the smallest set of the most likely tokens whose cumulative probability is greater than or equal to 0.8 is retained as the candidate set.  
     * The value range is (0, 1.0). A higher value increases randomness in generation; a lower value increases determinism.

TopP.description:
Used to control the randomness and diversity of model responses.  
> - Specifically, the temperature value controls the degree of smoothing applied to the probability distribution over candidate words during text generation. A higher temperature reduces the peak of the probability distribution, allowing more low-probability words to be selected, resulting in more diverse outputs. A lower temperature sharpens the peak, making high-probability words more likely to be selected, leading to more deterministic outputs.  
> - Value range: [0, 2). A value of 0 is not recommended because it is meaningless.

TopP.description:
Controls the randomness and diversity of model responses.  
> - Specifically, the temperature value controls the degree of smoothing applied to the probability distribution over candidate tokens during text generation. A higher temperature reduces the peakiness of the distribution, allowing lower-probability tokens to be selected more often, resulting in more diverse outputs. Conversely, a lower temperature sharpens the distribution, making high-probability tokens more likely to be chosen, leading to more deterministic outputs.  
> - Value range: [0, 2). A value of 0 is not recommended because it is meaningless.
